```{r Step 1, Inspect Job Satisfaction, include=TRUE}
?racecen1
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Inspect job satisfaction
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Frequency distribution

satjob_distribution <- gss_jqi_analysis %>%
  count(satjob) %>%
  mutate(
    pct = 100 * n / sum(n)
  )

print(satjob_distribution)


# Distribution by year

satjob_by_year <- gss_jqi_analysis %>%
  filter(!is.na(satjob)) %>%
  count(year, satjob) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  mutate(
    pct = 100 * n / sum(n)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

print(satjob_by_year, n = 100)

gss_jqi_analysis <- gss_jqi_analysis %>%
  mutate(
    job_satisfaction = case_when(
      satjob == 1 ~ 4,  # Very satisfied
      satjob == 2 ~ 3,  # Moderately satisfied
      satjob == 3 ~ 2,  # A little dissatisfied
      satjob == 4 ~ 1,  # Very dissatisfied
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Analysis sample
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Keep observations with both JQI and job satisfaction

jqi_satjob <- gss_jqi_analysis %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(jqi_z),
    !is.na(satjob)
  )

# Basic sample size

jqi_satjob %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    n_years = n_distinct(year),
    first_year = min(year),
    last_year = max(year)
  )

table(gss_jqi_analysis$satjob, useNA = "ifany")
attr(gss_jqi_analysis$satjob, "labels")


lm(job_satisfaction ~ jqi_z, data = jqi_satjob)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Pooled descriptive statistics
# ------------------------------------------------------------

pooled_descriptives <- jqi_satjob %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),

    jqi_mean = mean(jqi_z),
    jqi_sd = sd(jqi_z),

    satjob_mean = mean(satjob),
    satjob_sd = sd(satjob),

    pearson_r = cor(
      jqi_z,
      satjob,
      method = "pearson"
    ),

    spearman_rho = cor(
      jqi_z,
      satjob,
      method = "spearman"
    )
  )

print(pooled_descriptives)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Pooled Pearson correlation with confidence interval
# ------------------------------------------------------------

pooled_cor_test <- cor.test(
  jqi_satjob$jqi_z,
  jqi_satjob$job_satisfaction,
  method = "pearson"
)

print(pooled_cor_test)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Pooled Spearman correlation with confidence interval
# ------------------------------------------------------------

pooled_spearman_test <- cor.test(
  jqi_satjob$jqi_z,
  jqi_satjob$job_satisfaction,
  method = "spearman",
  exact = FALSE
)

print(pooled_spearman_test)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Pooled descriptive regression
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# This is descriptive, not a causal model.

m_satjob_pooled <- lm(
 job_satisfaction ~ jqi_z,
  data = jqi_satjob
)

summary(m_satjob_pooled)


# Tidy regression output

pooled_regression <- tidy(
  m_satjob_pooled,
  conf.int = TRUE
)

print(pooled_regression)

# 8. Year-specific correlations
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Pearson correlations by GSS year

yearly_pearson <- jqi_satjob %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),

    pearson_r = cor(
      jqi_z,
      job_satisfaction,
      method = "pearson"
    ),

    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(yearly_pearson, n = 30)


# Spearman correlations by GSS year

yearly_spearman <- jqi_satjob %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),

    spearman_rho = cor(
      jqi_z,
      job_satisfaction,
      method = "spearman"
    ),

    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(yearly_spearman, n = 30)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. Year-specific correlation tests and confidence intervals
# ------------------------------------------------------------

yearly_cor_tests <- jqi_satjob %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  group_modify(
    ~{
      test <- cor.test(
        .x$jqi_z,
        .x$job_satisfaction,
        method = "pearson"
      )

      tibble(
        n = nrow(.x),
        r = unname(test$estimate),
        p_value = test$p.value,
        conf_low = test$conf.int[1],
        conf_high = test$conf.int[2]
      )
    }
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

print(yearly_cor_tests, n = 30)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 10. Year-specific descriptive regressions
# ------------------------------------------------------------

yearly_models <- jqi_satjob %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  group_modify(
    ~tidy(
      lm(
        job_satisfaction ~ jqi_z,
        data = .x
      ),
      conf.int = TRUE
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(term == "jqi_z") %>%
  select(
    year,
    estimate,
    std.error,
    statistic,
    p.value,
    conf.low,
    conf.high
  )

print(yearly_models, n = 30)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 11. Descriptive job satisfaction by JQI quartile
# ------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_satjob_quartiles <- jqi_satjob %>%
  mutate(
    jqi_quartile = ntile(jqi_z, 4)
  ) %>%
  group_by(jqi_quartile) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_jqi = mean(jqi_z),
    mean_satjob = mean(job_satisfaction),
    sd_satjob = sd(job_satisfaction),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(jqi_satjob_quartiles)

#Workers in the lowest-quality employment environments report substantially lower job satisfaction, while satisfaction is relatively similar across the upper three quartiles of objective job quality. Objective job quality is associated with job satisfaction in a nonlinear fashion. Satisfaction increases with objective job quality through the lower and middle portions of the JQI distribution, reaches a maximum at approximately 0.5 standard deviations above the mean, and then declines somewhat at higher levels of objective job quality. The quadratic specification significantly improves fit over a linear specification.

m_satjob_quartile <- lm(
  job_satisfaction ~ factor(jqi_quartile),
  data = jqi_satjob %>%
    mutate(jqi_quartile = ntile(jqi_z, 4))
)

summary(m_satjob_quartile)

m_satjob_quadratic <- lm(
  job_satisfaction ~ jqi_z + I(jqi_z^2),
  data = jqi_satjob
)

summary(m_satjob_quadratic)

broom::tidy(
  m_satjob_quadratic,
  conf.int = TRUE
)

anova(m_satjob_pooled, m_satjob_quadratic)

quadratic_regression <- broom::tidy(
  m_satjob_quadratic,
  conf.int = TRUE
)

print(quadratic_regression)


b <- coef(m_satjob_quadratic)

turning_point <- -b["jqi_z"] / (2 * b["I(jqi_z^2)"])

turning_point

predicted_max <- predict(
  m_satjob_quadratic,
  newdata = data.frame(jqi_z = turning_point)
)

predicted_max

range(jqi_satjob$jqi_z, na.rm = TRUE)


# ============================================================
# Year-Specific Quadratic Models:
# Objective Job Quality and Job Satisfaction
# ============================================================

yearly_quadratic_models <- jqi_satjob %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  group_modify(~ {

    # Fit quadratic model
    model <- lm(
      job_satisfaction ~ jqi_z + I(jqi_z^2),
      data = .x
    )

    # Extract coefficients
    coefs <- broom::tidy(
      model,
      conf.int = TRUE
    )

    # Linear coefficient
    linear <- coefs %>%
      filter(term == "jqi_z")

    # Quadratic coefficient
    quadratic <- coefs %>%
      filter(term == "I(jqi_z^2)")

    # Calculate turning point
    beta1 <- coef(model)["jqi_z"]
    beta2 <- coef(model)["I(jqi_z^2)"]

    turning_point <- -beta1 / (2 * beta2)

    # Observed JQI range in this year
    jqi_min <- min(.x$jqi_z, na.rm = TRUE)
    jqi_max <- max(.x$jqi_z, na.rm = TRUE)

    # Predicted satisfaction at turning point
    predicted_at_turning_point <- predict(
      model,
      newdata = data.frame(jqi_z = turning_point)
    )

    # Model fit
    model_summary <- summary(model)

    tibble(
      n = nrow(.x),

      # Linear term
      linear_estimate = linear$estimate,
      linear_se = linear$std.error,
      linear_p = linear$p.value,
      linear_conf_low = linear$conf.low,
      linear_conf_high = linear$conf.high,

      # Quadratic term
      quadratic_estimate = quadratic$estimate,
      quadratic_se = quadratic$std.error,
      quadratic_p = quadratic$p.value,
      quadratic_conf_low = quadratic$conf.low,
      quadratic_conf_high = quadratic$conf.high,

      # Turning point
      turning_point = turning_point,
      predicted_satisfaction_at_turning_point =
        as.numeric(predicted_at_turning_point),

      # Empirical range
      jqi_min = jqi_min,
      jqi_max = jqi_max,

      # Is turning point within observed support?
      turning_point_in_range =
        turning_point >= jqi_min &
        turning_point <= jqi_max,

      # Model fit
      r_squared = model_summary$r.squared,
      adj_r_squared = model_summary$adj.r.squared
    )
  }) %>%
  ungroup()


# Print results
print(yearly_quadratic_models, n = 30)
yearly_quadratic_models
write_csv(
  yearly_quadratic_models,
  here(
    "04_figures",
    "yearly_quadratic_jqi_job_satisfaction.csv"
  )
)

yearly_quadratic_summary <- yearly_quadratic_models %>%
  select(
    year,
    n,
    quadratic_estimate,
    quadratic_se,
    quadratic_p,
    turning_point,
    predicted_satisfaction_at_turning_point,
    jqi_min,
    jqi_max,
    turning_point_in_range,
    r_squared
  )

print(yearly_quadratic_summary, n = 30)

yearly_quadratic_models %>%
  summarise(
    years = n(),
    negative_quadratic = sum(quadratic_estimate < 0),
    positive_quadratic = sum(quadratic_estimate > 0),
    significant_negative = sum(
      quadratic_estimate < 0 & quadratic_p < .05
    ),
    turning_points_in_range = sum(turning_point_in_range)
  )

yearly_quadratic_models %>% summarise( years = n(), negative_quadratic = sum(quadratic_estimate < 0), positive_quadratic = sum(quadratic_estimate > 0), significant_negative = sum( quadratic_estimate < 0 & quadratic_p < .05 ), turning_points_in_range = sum(turning_point_in_range) )

print(
  yearly_quadratic_models %>%
    select(
      year,
      n,
      linear_estimate,
      linear_p,
      quadratic_estimate,
      quadratic_p,
      turning_point,
      jqi_min,
      jqi_max,
      turning_point_in_range,
      r_squared
    ),
  n = 30
)

yearly_quadratic_models %>%
  summarise(
    years = n(),
    negative_quadratic = sum(quadratic_estimate < 0),
    positive_quadratic = sum(quadratic_estimate > 0),
    significant_negative = sum(
      quadratic_estimate < 0 & quadratic_p < .05
    ),
    turning_points_in_range = sum(turning_point_in_range)
  )

yearly_linear_ci <- yearly_quadratic_models %>%
  select(
    year,
    estimate = linear_estimate,
    conf_low = linear_conf_low,
    conf_high = linear_conf_high
  )

annual_linear_models <- ggplot(
  yearly_linear_ci,
  aes(x = year, y = estimate)
) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(
      ymin = conf_low,
      ymax = conf_high
    ),
    width = 0.15
  ) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = yearly_linear_ci$year
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "GSS year",
    y = "JQI coefficient",
    title = "Association between objective job quality and job satisfaction",
    subtitle = "Year-specific linear estimates with 95% confidence intervals"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggsave(
  here("04_figures", "annuallinearmodelplots.png"),
  plot = annual_linear_models
)

yearly_quadratic_ci <- yearly_quadratic_models %>%
  select(
    year,
    estimate = quadratic_estimate,
    conf_low = quadratic_conf_low,
    conf_high = quadratic_conf_high
  )

annual_quadratic_models <- ggplot(
  yearly_quadratic_ci,
  aes(x = year, y = estimate)
) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(
      ymin = conf_low,
      ymax = conf_high
    ),
    width = 0.15
  ) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = yearly_quadratic_ci$year
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "GSS year",
    y = "Quadratic JQI coefficient",
    title = "Nonlinearity in the association between job quality and job satisfaction",
    subtitle = "Year-specific quadratic estimates with 95% confidence intervals"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggsave(
  here("04_figures", "AnnualizedQuadraticModels.png"),
  plot = annual_quadratic_models
)

#There is recurring evidence of diminishing returns to objective job quality for job satisfaction, although the strength of the curvature varies substantially across survey years. There is recurring evidence of diminishing returns to objective job quality for job satisfaction, although the strength of the curvature varies substantially across survey years.

# 12. Figure: pooled relationship

loess_curve <- ggplot(jqi_satjob, aes(x = jqi_z, y = job_satisfaction)) +
  geom_jitter(
    width = 0,
    height = 0.08,
    alpha = 0.08
  ) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "loess",
    se = TRUE,
    span = 0.9

  labs(
    x = "Objective Job Quality Index (standardized)",
    y = "Job Satisfaction",
    title = "Objective Job Quality and Job Satisfaction",
    subtitle = "LOESS-smoothed descriptive association"

  theme_minimal()

ggsave(

)
```
